**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a snack or side of avocado halves, photographed from directly above on a white square plate.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The square plate spans roughly 25-26 cm edge to edge, so I use a 26 cm diameter equivalent. Vessel area = 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 531 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Two pieces of avocado, each a half-avocado section with skin still on one side. No oil, dressing, or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Piece 1 (longer, upper) covers about 6% of the plate. Piece 2 (lower right) covers about 5%. Food covers roughly 11% of the plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:**
- Piece 1: ~30 cm² x ~3 cm ≈ 90 ml
- Piece 2: ~28 cm² x ~3 cm ≈ 84 ml

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Avocado flesh is dense, but these pieces are partly hollow and irregular, so I use 0.8 g/ml.
- Piece 1: 90 x 0.8 ≈ 72 g
- Piece 2: 84 x 0.8 ≈ 67 g
- Total ≈ 139 g

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Avocado is about 160 kcal per 100 g.
- Piece 1: 72 g x 1.6 ≈ 115 kcal
- Piece 2: 67 g x 1.6 ≈ 107 kcal
- Total ≈ 222 kcal

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Two half-avocado pieces covering about a tenth of a dinner plate, weighing roughly 140 g in total, is plausible. A whole avocado is about 150-200 g with pit and skin, so this is consistent.
